title: I Let the Community-Studio Shelf Fee Catch the Resident Who Hoarded

parts.text: I paid a monthly shelf at the community art studio and found three unlabeled bins in mine. The shelf fee sheet the resident artist posted said: ONE SHELF PER FEE. UNLABELED BINS GO TO LOST-AND-FOUND. I was thirty-six, night painter, holding a wet panel with nowhere to dry. Resident Ollie said, "Residents overflow." I pointed at the sheet. He smiled. "Overflow is rent." I photographed the bins, the sheet, and my receipt. Then I moved the unlabeled bins to lost-and-found as the sheet described and logged the fee. At 7:22 the director asked why Ollie's name was on a shelf-hoard ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The director can see three unlabeled bins billed to my one paid shelf.

social.video_title: The resident hoarded my paid studio shelf — Part 1/2
social.description: Wet panel, three mystery bins, and a fee sheet he posted. I followed lost-and-found. Would you have stacked the floor?

parts.text: Ollie called it a mixup until lost-and-found tagged his glaze. I printed the ticket, the sheet, and the photo. My panel dried. Ollie paid a second shelf and told the loft the sheet was always about optics. Optics is a word residents use when glaze is in a still. Shelf policy now has a second line: OVERFLOW PAYS. I keep one. Ollie labels. The rack finally has air.

social.video_title: Overflow pays for a second shelf — Part 2/2
social.description: Hoard ticket, a second fee, and a second line on the sheet. Was rent ever my receipt?
